summary: "Journal des Goncourt (Deuxième volume)" by Edmond de Goncourt and Jules de Goncourt is a diary written between 1850 and 1896. This candid chronicle captures the bitter rivalries and fragile friendships of Parisian literary and artistic society. Written through an unusual collaborative process the brothers called "dual dictation," the Journal records intimate conversations, professional jealousies, and personal disappointments with startling honesty. Their unflinching portrayals of famous contemporaries—including Zola, Flaubert, and Baudelaire—strained friendships and sparked controversy, making publication contentious for decades.
